decks.name: After Toaplan
decks.note: Toaplan closed in 1994 and its programmers went on to Raizing and later Cave. Batsugun, then the Raizing games, then Yagawa's two Cave games.
decks.author: Shmup Deck

decks.name: Bomb everything
decks.note: Older verticals where bombs are plentiful and saving them is a mistake.
decks.author: Shmup Deck

decks.name: Easy tate
decks.note: Vertical shooters that are kind to a first credit, for getting used to the turned screen.
decks.author: Shmup Deck

decks.name: Every Cave game
decks.note: Cave's own shooters, oldest first. Black Labels and arrange versions left out.
decks.author: Shmup Deck

decks.name: Five steps into danmaku
decks.note: Five Cave games, one idea each: DonPachi's laser, DoDonPachi's chain, Feveron's speed, ESP Ra.De.'s bullet reading, Ketsui's lock-on. Play them in this order.
decks.author: Shmup Deck

decks.name: Konami tate
decks.note: Five Konami verticals that turn the monitor clockwise, the other way from Cave and Toaplan. On a cab set up for those, use the core's flip option.
decks.author: Shmup Deck

decks.name: Learn to chain
decks.note: Cave's scoring systems in the order they appeared. Each game changes what a chain is, so each one is practice for the next.
decks.author: Shmup Deck

decks.name: Psikyo
decks.note: Psikyo's shooters from Samurai Aces to Dragon Blaze, in release order.
decks.author: Shmup Deck

decks.name: Raiden
decks.note: Seibu Kaihatsu's Raiden games in order, with Viper Phase 1, the first shooter on their SPI board, where it falls.
decks.author: Shmup Deck

decks.name: Raizing
decks.note: Everything Raizing made, in release order, including the two it made for Capcom as Eighting: Dimahoo and 1944.
decks.author: Shmup Deck

decks.name: Toaplan
decks.note: Toaplan's vertical shooters in release order, Tiger Heli in 1985 to Batsugun in 1993.
decks.author: Shmup Deck

decks.name: Two players
decks.note: Shooters worth playing with someone next to you. All ten take two at once.
decks.author: Shmup Deck
